name: Mary, the mother of Jesus
charge: Be it unto me according to thy word; blessed is she that believed
summary: A virgin of Nazareth, espoused, was told she would conceive by the Holy Ghost and bear the Son of the Highest, and that with God nothing shall be impossible. She answered, Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word. Elisabeth's word to her is the verdict: blessed is she that believed. Her own song says all generations shall call her blessed, and they have.
offense: And Mary said, Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word. She arose in those days and went into the hill country with haste to Elisabeth. She kept all these things, and pondered them in her heart. When the days of her purification according to the law of Moses were accomplished, they brought him to Jerusalem, to present him to the Lord; as it is written in the law of the Lord. At Cana her word to the servants was the rule she lived by: Whatsoever he saith unto you, do it. She stood by the cross.
judgment: Hail, thou that art highly favoured, the Lord is with thee: blessed art thou among women. Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb. And blessed is she that believed: for there shall be a performance of those things which were told her from the Lord. My soul doth magnify the Lord, and my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour. For he hath regarded the low estate of his handmaiden: for, behold, from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed. From the cross her Son gave her to the disciple he loved, and from that hour that disciple took her unto his own home.

entries.commentary: A decree from Caesar Augustus sends every man to his own city to be taxed, and Joseph goes up to Bethlehem because he was of the house and lineage of David. She brought forth her firstborn son, and wrapped him in swaddling clothes, and laid him in a manger, because there was no room for them in the inn.

The angel gives the shepherds a sign: ye shall find the babe wrapped in swaddling clothes, lying in a manger. The swaddling clothes are the mark of an ordinary entrance into life. The wise man says plainly that there is no king that had any other beginning of birth.
The shepherds come with haste, find Mary and Joseph and the babe, and make known abroad what was told them concerning this child. Mary kept all these things, and pondered them in her heart.
When eight days were accomplished for the circumcising of the child, his name was called Jesus. He was born under the law and everything done for him was done after the law.
When the days of her purification were accomplished they brought him to Jerusalem to present him to the Lord, and to offer a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons, as it is written in the law.

Simeon was just and devout, waiting for the consolation of Israel, and it was revealed unto him that he should not see death before he had seen the Lord's Christ. Behold, this child is set for the fall and rising again of many in Israel, and for a sign which shall be spoken against.

Anna, a prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Aser, departed not from the temple, but served God with fastings and prayers night and day. She is named by her tribe. Asher was still there in that day, and she spake of him to all them that looked for redemption in Jerusalem.

His parents went to Jerusalem every year at the feast of the passover, and at twelve years old he tarried behind, and was found in the temple sitting in the midst of the doctors, both hearing them and asking them questions. Wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business? They understood not the saying. He went down with them, and came to Nazareth, and was subject unto them. He was raised under his parents and under the law, and increased in wisdom and stature, and in favour with God and man.

At the marriage in Cana his mother tells him they have no wine, and though he answers, Mine hour is not yet come, she tells the servants, Whatsoever he saith unto you, do it. She knew what he could do. The governor of the feast says every man sets forth good wine first, and the worse afterward, but thou hast kept the good wine until now. What was made was better than what had been served. This beginning of miracles did Jesus in Cana of Galilee, and manifested forth his glory; and his disciples believed on him.

He made a scourge of small cords and drove them all out of the temple, with the sheep and the oxen, poured out the changers' money and overthrew the tables. He drove grown men out with a whip. Take these things hence; make not my Father's house an house of merchandise. No man had business trading in there at the passover. His disciples remembered that it was written, The zeal of thine house hath eaten me up. He was fulfilling what David had written.

They ask what sign he shews. Asking after signs was their habit, and the epistle names it. Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up. It went over their heads, and they answered with the forty and six years of building. He spake of the temple of his body. The Most High does not dwell in temples made with hands, and the body itself is called a temple in the scriptures. The saying was kept and used against him later by false witnesses at his trial.
Many believed when they saw the miracles, but he did not commit himself unto them, for he knew all men, and needed not that any should testify of man: for he knew what was in man.

In the days of Ahaz, son of Jotham, son of Uzziah, king of Judah, Rezin king of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel went up toward Jerusalem to war, but could not prevail against it. It was told the house of David that Syria was confederate with Ephraim, and the heart of Ahaz and his people was moved as the trees of the wood are moved with the wind.

The Most High told Isaiah to go meet Ahaz, he and his son Shearjashub, at the end of the conduit of the upper pool, in the highway of the fuller's field. Isaiah was to say, "Take heed, and be quiet; fear not, neither be fainthearted," for the two tails of these smoking firebrands, the fierce anger of Rezin with Syria and of Remaliah's son.

Syria, Ephraim, and Remaliah's son took evil counsel, saying, "Let us go up against Judah, and vex it, and set a king in the midst of it, even the son of Tabeal." The Most High says it shall not stand nor come to pass, for the head of Syria is Damascus and the head of Damascus is Rezin, meaning the capital. Deacon Nadan taught that the sign here is Isaiah's children, and Captain OC taught on the Samaritan woman being from Ephraim.

Within threescore and five years Ephraim shall be broken, that it be not a people; the head of Ephraim is Samaria and the head of Samaria is Remaliah's son. "If ye will not believe, surely ye shall not be established."

The Most High spoke again to Ahaz, telling him to ask a sign, whether in the depth or in the height above. Ahaz said, "I will not ask, neither will I tempt the LORD." Isaiah answered, "Hear ye now, O house of David; Is it a small thing for you to weary men, but will ye weary my God also?"

"Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel." The sign is the child, not the virgin herself. Many think the virgin was the sign, and that leads into all types of false doctrine; the virgin is simply a woman of age to be married. Captain OC opened how christianity stumbles over the word seed. -

"Butter and honey shall he eat, that he may know to refuse the evil, and choose the good." Before the child shall know to refuse evil and choose good, the land that Ahaz abhorred shall be forsaken of both her kings.
The Most High shall bring upon Ahaz, his people, and his father's house days that have not come since Ephraim departed from Judah, even the king of Assyria.

In that day the Most High shall hiss for the fly in the rivers of Egypt and the bee in the land of Assyria, and they shall come and rest in the desolate valleys, in the holes of the rocks, upon all thorns and bushes. In the same day the Most High shall shave with a hired razor, the king of Assyria, the head and the hair of the feet, and consume the beard.
In that day a man shall nourish a young cow and two sheep, and for the abundance of milk they give he shall eat butter; butter and honey shall everyone eat that is left in the land.

Every place where there were a thousand vines at a thousand silverlings shall become briers and thorns, and men shall come there with arrows and bows because all the land is briers and thorns. The hills digged with the mattock shall not be entered for fear of briers and thorns, but shall be for the sending forth of oxen and the treading of lesser cattle.

verses.text: And in the sixth month the angel Gabriel was sent from God unto a city of Galilee, named Nazareth,
To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin’s name was Mary.
And the angel came in unto her, and said, Hail, thou that art highly favoured, the Lord is with thee: blessed art thou among women.
And when she saw him, she was troubled at his saying, and cast in her mind what manner of salutation this should be.
And the angel said unto her, Fear not, Mary: for thou hast found favour with God.
And, behold, thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son, and shalt call his name JESUS.
He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David:
And he shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever; and of his kingdom there shall be no end.
Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?

And the angel answered and said unto her, The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God.
And, behold, thy cousin Elisabeth, she hath also conceived a son in her old age: and this is the sixth month with her, who was called barren.
For with God nothing shall be impossible.
And Mary said, Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word. And the angel departed from her.
And Mary arose in those days, and went into the hill country with haste, into a city of Juda;
And entered into the house of Zacharias, and saluted Elisabeth.
And it came to pass, that, when Elisabeth heard the salutation of Mary, the babe leaped in her womb; and Elisabeth was filled with the Holy Ghost:
And she spake out with a loud voice, and said, Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb.
And whence is this to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?
For, lo, as soon as the voice of thy salutation sounded in mine ears, the babe leaped in my womb for joy.
And blessed is she that believed: for there shall be a performance of those things which were told her from the Lord.
And Mary said, My soul doth magnify the Lord,
And my spirit hath rejoiced in God my Saviour.
For he hath regarded the low estate of his handmaiden: for, behold, from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed.
For he that is mighty hath done to me great things; and holy is his name.
And his mercy is on them that fear him from generation to generation.
He hath shewed strength with his arm; he hath scattered the proud in the imagination of their hearts.
He hath put down the mighty from their seats, and exalted them of low degree.
He hath filled the hungry with good things; and the rich he hath sent empty away.
He hath holpen his servant Israel, in remembrance of his mercy;
As he spake to our fathers, to Abraham, and to his seed for ever.
But Mary kept all these things, and pondered them in her heart.
And when the days of her purification according to the law of Moses were accomplished, they brought him to Jerusalem, to present him to the Lord;
(As it is written in the law of the Lord, Every male that openeth the womb shall be called holy to the Lord;)
And to offer a sacrifice according to that which is said in the law of the Lord, A pair of turtledoves, or two young pigeons.
And the third day there was a marriage in Cana of Galilee; and the mother of Jesus was there:
And both Jesus was called, and his disciples, to the marriage.
And when they wanted wine, the mother of Jesus saith unto him, They have no wine.
Jesus saith unto her, Woman, what have I to do with thee? mine hour is not yet come.
His mother saith unto the servants, Whatsoever he saith unto you, do it.
Now there stood by the cross of Jesus his mother, and his mother’s sister, Mary the wife of Cleophas, and Mary Magdalene.
When Jesus therefore saw his mother, and the disciple standing by, whom he loved, he saith unto his mother, Woman, behold thy son!
Then saith he to the disciple, Behold thy mother! And from that hour that disciple took her unto his own home.
Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.
